title: How did Apple’s three cash activities reconcile to its cash balance?
introduction: Classify each movement as Operating, Investing, or Financing; then read its direction and magnitude. The sign shows where cash moved, not whether the activity was good or bad.

cash-generated-by-operating-activities.helper: Cash connected to Apple’s main business operations.

purchases-of-marketable-securities.helper: Cash used to buy marketable securities.

maturities-of-marketable-securities.reportedLabel: Proceeds from maturities of marketable securities

sales-of-marketable-securities.reportedLabel: Proceeds from sales of marketable securities

payments-for-property-plant-and-equipmen.reportedLabel: Payments for acquisition of property, plant and equipment
payments-for-property-plant-and-equipmen.helper: Cash invested in long-term operating assets.

other-investing-activities.helper: Apple’s remaining reported Investing cash flow.

taxes-related-to-net-share-settlement.reportedLabel: Payments for taxes related to net share settlement of equity awards
taxes-related-to-net-share-settlement.helper: Cash paid in connection with employee equity awards.

dividends-and-dividend-equivalents.reportedLabel: Payments for dividends and dividend equivalents
dividends-and-dividend-equivalents.helper: Cash paid to shareholders through dividends.

common-stock-repurchases.helper: Cash used to buy back Apple shares.

term-debt-issuance-net.reportedLabel: Proceeds from issuance of term debt, net
term-debt-issuance-net.helper: Cash received from new term debt, net of issuance effects.

term-debt-repayment.helper: Cash used to repay term debt.

commercial-paper-net.reportedLabel: Proceeds from/(Repayments of) commercial paper, net
commercial-paper-net.helper: The net cash effect of Apple’s short-term commercial paper.

other-financing-activities.helper: Apple’s remaining reported Financing cash flow.

net-change-in-cash.reportedLabel: Increase in cash, cash equivalents, and restricted cash and cash equivalents
net-change-in-cash.helper: The reported change after all three activity sections.

activityDescriptions.operating: Cash connected to the main business operations.
activityDescriptions.investing: Cash connected to securities and long-term assets.
activityDescriptions.financing: Cash connected to creditors and owners.

signBoundary: An inflow or outflow describes cash direction, not quality. Context is required before judging the activity.
fxBoundary: A reported net change in cash may include exchange-rate effects, depending on the filing taxonomy. For this reviewed Apple record, the three reported activity totals reconcile exactly to the reported change; FinPath does not generalize that identity or claim exchange-rate effects were zero.
remainingBoundary: A positive or negative section total is not automatically good or bad. Inspect the underlying activities and business context.

finalQuestion.prompt: Where does Apple report PP&E purchases and share repurchases?
finalQuestion.hint: Choose one. This is practice, not a score.
finalQuestion.supportedFeedback: Yes. Apple reports PP&E purchases in Investing and share repurchases in Financing.
finalQuestion.unsupportedFeedback: Apple reports PP&E purchases in Investing because they acquire long-term assets; share repurchases are transactions with owners, so they appear in Financing.

boundaries.operating: Operating Cash Flow is not the same as the annual change in Apple’s cash balance.
boundaries.investing: Positive or negative Investing cash flow is not automatically good or bad. The underlying activities and context matter.
boundaries.financing: Positive or negative Financing cash flow is not automatically good or bad. It shows cash flows connected to creditors and owners.

verification.unitNote: Apple reports this statement in USD millions. FinPath displays large figures in USD billions.

sources.title: Apple FY2025 Form 10-K — Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows
